ranked_remaining_gates.label: Voicemail action-only behavior
ranked_remaining_gates.why: It is the smallest remaining English product-policy gate after autonomy: one known voicemail case, explicit owner feedback, and no regulated knowledge or broad classifier expansion.
ranked_remaining_gates.risk: Could make the runtime take inappropriate same-loop actions after voicemail detection or blur message-taking versus selling behavior.
ranked_remaining_gates.next_action: Open a synthetic English voicemail action-only policy probe before any runtime patch.
ranked_remaining_gates.review_question: No new review needed unless the probe finds ambiguity in action-only voicemail behavior.

ranked_remaining_gates.label: Coverage knowledge-policy behavior
ranked_remaining_gates.why: It involves regulated coverage or eligibility implications and needs product/legal knowledge boundaries before runtime work.
ranked_remaining_gates.risk: Could imply insurance coverage, eligibility, or legal/financial advice without a reviewed knowledge policy.
ranked_remaining_gates.next_action: Keep blocked until a separate knowledge-policy checkpoint defines allowed facts, uncertainty handling, and escalation.
ranked_remaining_gates.review_question: Should coverage behavior wait behind the lower-blast-radius voicemail gate?

ranked_remaining_gates.label: Customer-move classification outside selected non-refusal groups
ranked_remaining_gates.why: It has the highest blast radius because it changes reachability across multiple runtime branches.
ranked_remaining_gates.risk: Could route customer turns into newly promoted behavior without enough evidence for each branch.
ranked_remaining_gates.next_action: Keep blocked until smaller policy gates provide clearer acceptance criteria for broader classifier reachability.
ranked_remaining_gates.review_question: Should broad classifier expansion remain last among the current English product-policy gates?
